To analyse how strong the effects of the connection on the biomass, biodiversity, and population densities within ecosystems were, we want to compile a dataset (`ds_metaecosystems_effect_size`) where each row represents the effect size of a connected vs unconnected ecosystem type (e.g., small autotrophic connected vs unconnected) at a time point. If the 95% CI of the effect size crosses the zero line it means that it is statistically significant. We use the effect size Hedge's d (aka Hedge's g), as it can handle the treatment and/or control equal to zero (log response ratio cannot: ln(treatment/0) = Inf; ln(0/control) = -inf; ln(0/0) = Nan), small sample sizes ("*it works well when there are as few as five to ten studies",* @Rosenberg2013), and unequal variance between treatment and control ([@Rosenberg2013]). Hedge's d (d) is the difference in mean between treatment and control divided by by their weighted spread (denominator) multiplied by a factor (J) that controls for small sample sizes [@Rosenberg2013]. The 95% confidence interval of Hedge's d is calculated from its standard error (SE) as [@Hedges1985] $d ± 1.96 * SE$ where the standard error is calculated as show in @Borenstein2009.

We calculate Hedge's d and its 95 % confidence interval in three steps. (1) Calculate means, standard deviations and sample sizes. Calculate the mean of the treatment (Y1) and control (Y2), the standard deviation of the treatment (s1) and the control (s2), as well as the sample size of the treatment (n1) and the control (n2) at each time point and for each response variable. (2) Calculate Hedge's d. Use means, standard deviations and sample sizes to calculate effect sizes. (3) Retain only the treatments (connected ecosystems), discarding the controls (unconnected). This is because we calculated the effect size of only connected compared to unconnected and not the other way around.

$$
d = \frac{Y1 - Y2}{denominator} * J
$$

$$
denominator = \sqrt{\frac{(n_1-1)*s_1^2 + (n_2 - 1) * s_2^2}{n_1 + n_2 - 2}}
$$

$$
J = 1 - \frac{3}{(4 * (n_1 + n_2 - 2)) - 1}
$$

$$
SE = \sqrt{J^2 * \frac{n_1 + n_2}{n_1*n_2} + \frac{d^2}{2*(n_1 + n_2)}}
$$

<br>

```{r}

## - (1) Calculate means, standard deviations and sample sizes. - ##

ds_metaecosystems_effect_size = list()

for (variable_i in 1:length(variables_metaecos)) {
  
  columns_to_group_by = colnames(ds_metaecosystems %>% 
                                   select(time_point,
                                          day,
                                          ecosystem_size_ml,
                                          connection,
                                          volume_disturbed_across_sizes))
  
  ds_metaecosystems_effect_size[[variable_i]] = ds_metaecosystems %>%
    filter(
      
    # To have a cleaner dataset filter out ecosystems in which this variable 
    # could not be computed (e.g., species richness of a crashed culture). 
      
      !is.na(!!sym(variables_metaecos[variable_i]))) %>%
    
    # To afterwards calculate effect sizes, get the mean, sd, and sample size 
    # of treatments at each time point 
    
    group_by(across(all_of(columns_to_group_by))) %>%
    summarise(across(all_of(variables_metaecos[variable_i]),
                     list(mean = mean,
                          sd = sd)),
              sample_size = n()) %>%
    
    # To know of which variable the sample size is when you afterwards bind 
    # columns, add the name of the variable to the name of the sample size column. 
    
    rename_with( ~ paste0(variables_metaecos[variable_i], 
                          "_sample_size"),
                 matches("sample_size"))
}

# To have in the rows treatment and in the columns means, sd, and sample size, bind columns together. 

ds_metaecosystems_effect_size <- reduce(ds_metaecosystems_effect_size,
                                        full_join,
                                        by = columns_to_group_by) %>%
  mutate(metaecosystem_type = paste0(ecosystem_size_ml, "_", volume_disturbed_across_sizes, "_", connection))
```

```{r}

## - Calculate Hedge's d. - ##

# Initialise the effect size columns 

for (variable_i in length(variables_metaecos)) {
  ds_metaecosystems_effect_size <- ds_metaecosystems_effect_size %>%
    mutate(!!paste0(variables_metaecos[variable_i], "_d") := NA,
           !!paste0(variables_metaecos[variable_i], "_d_upper") := NA,
           !!paste0(variables_metaecos[variable_i], "_d_lower") := NA)
}
  
row_n = 0

# For each treatment at each time point, calculate effect size and 95% CI

for (treatment_i in 1:nrow(treatments_and_controls_metaecos)) {
    
  for (time_i in 1:length(time_points_for_ES)) {
    
    row_n = row_n + 1
    
    treatment_row = ds_metaecosystems_effect_size %>%
      filter(metaecosystem_type == treatments_and_controls_metaecos$treatment[treatment_i],
             time_point == time_points_for_ES[time_i])
      
    control_row = ds_metaecosystems_effect_size %>%
      filter(metaecosystem_type == treatments_and_controls_metaecos$control[treatment_i],
             time_point == time_points_for_ES[time_i])
      
      for (variable_i in 1:length(variables_metaecos)) {
        
        hedges_d = calculate.hedges_d(
          treatment_row[[paste0(variables_metaecos[variable_i], "_mean")]],
          treatment_row[[paste0(variables_metaecos[variable_i], "_sd")]],
          treatment_row[[paste0(variables_metaecos[variable_i], "_sample_size")]],
          control_row[[paste0(variables_metaecos[variable_i], "_mean")]],
          control_row[[paste0(variables_metaecos[variable_i], "_sd")]],
          control_row[[paste0(variables_metaecos[variable_i], "_sample_size")]])
        
        ds_metaecosystems_effect_size[[paste0(variables_metaecos[variable_i], "_d")]][
          ds_metaecosystems_effect_size$metaecosystem_type ==
           treatments_and_controls_metaecos$treatment[treatment_i] &
          ds_metaecosystems_effect_size$time_point == 
           time_points_for_ES[time_i]] =
          hedges_d$d
        
        ds_metaecosystems_effect_size[[paste0(variables_metaecos[variable_i], "_d_upper")]][
          ds_metaecosystems_effect_size$metaecosystem_type ==
           treatments_and_controls_metaecos$treatment[treatment_i] &
          ds_metaecosystems_effect_size$time_point == 
           time_points_for_ES[time_i]] =
          hedges_d$upper_CI
        
        ds_metaecosystems_effect_size[[paste0(variables_metaecos[variable_i], "_d_lower")]][
          ds_metaecosystems_effect_size$metaecosystem_type ==
           treatments_and_controls_metaecos$treatment[treatment_i] &
          ds_metaecosystems_effect_size$time_point == 
           time_points_for_ES[time_i]] =
          hedges_d$lower_CI
        
      }
    }
  }
```

## - Retain only the connected ecosystems, discarding the controls (unconnected). - ##

ds_metaecosystems_effect_size = ds_metaecosystems_effect_size %>%
  filter(connection == "connected")
